title: React Native Small Examples
description: Use these small React Native examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Make a native screen
examples.description: A View groups native page parts. Text displays words.
examples.code:
import {View,Text} from "react-native";
export default function App(){return <View style={{padding:24}}><Text>Reading club</Text></View>;}
examples.output: The app screen shows Reading club with inner space around it.

examples.title: Create named styles
examples.output: The screen area has a pale background and a large bold title.

examples.title: Add a button and state
examples.description: React state remembers a value between renders.
examples.output: Each button press increases the visible number.

examples.title: Use a text input
examples.description: TextInput lets someone type text. onChangeText supplies the new text, so state can keep the field and screen together.
examples.code:
import {useState} from "react";import {View,Text,TextInput} from "react-native";
export default function App(){const [name,setName]=useState("");return <View style={{padding:24}}><Text>Your name</Text><TextInput accessibilityLabel="Your name" value={name} onChangeText={setName} style={{borderWidth:1,padding:12}}/><Text>Hello, {name}</Text></View>;}
examples.output: The greeting changes as a name is typed.

examples.title: Arrange a row with flex
examples.description: React Native uses Flexbox for layout. Its default direction is a column, so set row when items should sit beside each other.
examples.code:
import {View,Text} from "react-native";
export default function App(){return <View style={{padding:24,flexDirection:"row",gap:12}}><Text>Books read</Text><Text>4</Text></View>;}
examples.output: The label and count appear side by side with a gap.

examples.title: Scroll a small amount of content
examples.code:
import {ScrollView,Text} from "react-native";
export default function App(){return <ScrollView contentContainerStyle={{padding:24}}>{Array.from({length:20},(_,i)=><Text key={i} style={{padding:12}}>Reading tip {i+1}</Text>)}</ScrollView>;}
examples.output: The tips can scroll if they do not fit on the screen.

examples.title: Render a list efficiently
examples.description: FlatList receives data and a function for each row.
examples.output: The app shows one row per book with a stable id for each.

examples.title: Use a local image
examples.description: Image displays a native picture. A local file can be bundled with require so the app can include it at build time.
examples.code:
import {View,Image} from "react-native";
export default function App(){return <View style={{padding:24}}><Image source={require("./assets/garden.png")} style={{width:160,height:120}} accessibilityLabel="Our school garden"/></View>;}
examples.output: After adding a real garden.png file, the app shows it at the chosen size.

examples.title: Make a custom pressable control
examples.description: Pressable can wrap a custom control. Its style callback receives pressed, so the control can show a clear response.
examples.code:
import {Pressable,Text,View} from "react-native";
export default function App(){return <View style={{padding:24}}><Pressable accessibilityRole="button" onPress={()=>console.log("Chosen")} style={({pressed})=>({padding:16,backgroundColor:pressed?"#12345a":"#174a8b"})}><Text style={{color:"white"}}>Choose a book</Text></Pressable></View>;}
examples.output: The control darkens while pressed and logs Chosen when activated.

examples.title: Respect the safe screen area
examples.description: Some screens have cutouts or system bars.
examples.output: On a supported device, the content stays inside the safe area.

examples.title: Show an empty-list message
examples.description: A useful list explains when it has no items.
examples.code:
import {FlatList,Text} from "react-native";
export default function App(){return <FlatList data={[]} renderItem={({item})=><Text>{item.title}</Text>} ListEmptyComponent={<Text>Add your first book to begin.</Text>} contentContainerStyle={{padding:24}}/>;}
examples.output: The empty list shows a helpful next step instead of a blank screen.

examples.title: Make a local two-view demo
examples.description: State can choose between two simple views while learning.
examples.code:
import {useState} from "react";import {View,Text,Button} from "react-native";
export default function App(){const [detail,setDetail]=useState(false);return <View style={{padding:24}}>{detail?<><Text>Moon Trip is a space story.</Text><Button title="Back" onPress={()=>setDetail(false)}/></>:<><Text>Books</Text><Button title="Open Moon Trip" onPress={()=>setDetail(true)}/></>}</View>;}
examples.output: The buttons switch between a list label and a book detail view within local state.
